correctness.rationale: The precise map and isolate-point symbolic correspondence are supported by Saiki--Takahasi--Yorke Lemmas 2.4--2.6. For each n, right-visit cumulative parities form a bijective invertible linear transform of n word bits. The two singular-value powers equal A and n-A, with A an independent binomial count plus final parity. For real (even) parity the derivative is diagonal and eigen-gap=singular-gap; for odd parity it is signed offdiagonal with characteristic polynomial lambda²+2^n and eigen-gap=0. Binomial reflection symmetry gives identical singular-gap conditional distributions, except the omitted all-left word at the unique maximal gap. De Moivre--Laplace and a total-variation error 2^{-n} prove the coupled half-normal limit. The included checker executed successfully on 4083 words, verifying full rational periodic geometry for lengths <=8, but the infinite proof is analytic.

value.rationale: The originating research explicitly distinguishes periodic complex and real eigenvalue spectra in a model of twisting and nonuniform expansion. Rather than recounting eigenvalue classes, the finding establishes a complete finite-n *joint* classification of those classes by Euclidean singular anisotropy; exact histogram matching, a single geometrically forced defect and a coupled half-normal/atomic limit explain how complex conjugate eigenvalues of equal modulus can coexist with large transient stretching. This is a natural comparison of two non-equivalent derivative invariants at periodic points; it is neither a mere new parameter choice nor a trivial consequence of previously reported marginal statistics.
